Cs611 Assignment 1 Solution

A. Classification of Problems:
Problem 1: Users report that, during checkout, the total order cost is sometimes miscalculated and doesn't match the item prices in their cart.

Classification: Bug.

Problem 2: When a customer adds an item to their wishlist, the system occasionally crashes, and an error message appears.

Classification: Failure.

Problem 3: In the product catalog, some items have missing images, even though they were uploaded by the administrator.
Classification: Defect.
Problem 4: Customers have encountered an issue where, upon attempting to log in, the system does not recognize their credentials and returns an "Invalid username or password" message. This occurs intermittently.
Classification: Fault.
Problem 5: The search functionality works correctly most of the time, but occasionally it returns no results for valid queries.

Classification: Error
B. Explanation of Classification:
1. Bug (Problem 1):
A bug is a deviation from the expected behavior of the software. In this case, the miscalculation of the total order cost is a clear deviation from the expected behavior of the checkout process.
2. Failure (Problem 2):
A failure occurs when the software does not perform as intended in a specific scenario. In this case, the system crashing and displaying an error message when a customer adds an item to their Wishlist is a failure.
3. Defect (Problem 3):
A defect is a flaw or imperfection in the software. In this case, the missing images in the product catalog are a clear imperfection that needs to be addressed.
4. Fault (Problem 4):
A fault is a specific type of defect that may cause a failure. In this case, the system not recognizing valid credentials during login indicates a fault in the authenticating process.
5. Error (Problem 5):
An error is a human mistake made during the development process that leads to a defect. In this case, the occasional failure of the search functionally to return results for valid queries is likely due to an error in the code.
C. 	Proposed Solutions:

1. Bug (Problem 1) - Total order cost miscalculation:
Solution: Review the code responsible for calculating the total order cost. Perform thorough testing to identify and fix any mathematical or logical errors.
2. Failure (Problem 2) – System crash when adding item to Wishlist:
Solution: Investigate the code related to adding items to the Wishlist, Debug and fix the issue causing the system crash. Implement proper error handling to prevent crashes in the future.
3. Defect (Problem 3) – Missing images in product catalog:
Solution: Review the image uploading and retrieval process. Ensure that uploaded images are properly stored and displayed in the catalog. Implement error-checking mechanism to catch and handle missing images.

4. Fault (Problem 4) – Invalid credentials during login:
Solution: Review the authentication process and database interactions. Identify and rectify the fault causing the system to reject valid credentials intermittently. Implement robust error handling for login attempts.
5. Error (Problem 5) – Search functionality returning no results:
Solution: Review the code responsible for handling search queries. Identify and correct any logical or algorithmic errors that maybe causing valid queries to fail. Conduct thorough testing to ensure consistent functionality.

﻿As a project manager, it's important to consider the specific needs and priorities of the project when deciding how to allocate budget for software development. In the case of a software project for a bank, it's likely that security and performance would be among the top priorities.
Here are some reasons why these areas might be prioritized over the software user interface:
Security: Ensuring the security of financial transactions and sensitive customer Information is critical for a bank. Allocating more budget to security features can help to protect against cyber-attacks and other security threats.
Performance: The performance of the software is important for ensuring a seamless user experience and maintaining the trust of customers. Allocating more budget to performance-related features can help to ensure that the software operates smoothly and efficiently.
That being said, the software user interface is also an important consideration for a bank's software. A well-designed user interface can make it easier for customers to use the software and can improve the overall user experience. Ultimately. The best approach will depend on the specific needs and priorities of the project. It may be necessary to allocate more budget to one area over the others in order to ensure that the software meets the necessary quality standards.

Module-01: Software Quality Engineering Discipline

A. Quality Engineering Basics
What is software quality? What are the characteristics of high quality software solutions? What
defines quality? These are some of the subjective question in the field of Software Quality
Engineering. Modern Software Systems are usually interconnections of multiple underlying
software and due to lack of standardization and varied nature it’s really difficult to define
quality. Software Quality Engineering involves complete software development process just to
ensure that that any agreed-upon processes, standards and procedures are being followed to
get desired results and there should be no cherry picking of standards

B. Roles and Responsibility
People may have different expectations related to software quality assurance based on their
roles and responsibility. The stakeholders for software development are divided into two and
their expectations are as follows:

C. Consumer
Consumers of a software product are further categorized into the following:
   ● Users are the group which use the services acquired by the customer: The quality
     expectations on the side of users are as follows:
         o It performs all the functions as specified in the software requirements, which
             fits/meets the user’s needs.
         o Performs all the specified functions correctly over repeated use or over a long
             period of time, or performs its functions reliably.
   ● Customer usually acquire the Software and Services: The quality expectations on the
     side of consumer are as follows:
         o Basic expectations of the consumer are similar to that of users with additional
             concentration on the cost of the software solution.

D. Producer
Producer of the software solutions includes person involved in the development, management,
maintenance and service of the software product. It also includes third party software product
and organizations. For producers, the expectations are as follows:
   ● Their biggest concern is to fulfill their contractual obligations by producing software
     products that conform to product specifications.
   ● Proper choice of software methodologies, languages, tools, software usability and
     modifiability and other factors are closely related to quality for this category of
     stakeholders.
                                                                                      Page | 3

E. Off the Shelf Products
These are plug-and-play products and are usually known as Plugins. They are developed and
tested independently of Software Solutions. Their main purpose is to provide reusable
functionality. Off-the-shelf (OTS) software products can be defined as “software product(s)
available for any user, at cost or not, and used without the need to conduct development
activities”. Proper analysis should be perform while making decision regarding selection OTS as
one solution does not fit all.

   ISO-9126 Quality Framework
ISO-9126 is International Standard for Software Evaluation, it provides hierarchical framework
for quality definition, organized into quality characteristics. There are six top-level quality
characteristics that are summarized below:

F. Functionality
Functionality is the essential purpose of any product or service. The functionality characteristic
allows drawing conclusions about how well software provides and performs desired functions.
The functions are those that satisfy stated or implied needs. The more functions a product has,
e.g. a sale order processing system, then the more complicated it becomes to define it's
functionality. Continuing with the same example, the sales order system must be able to record
sales, price, quantity, tax, shipping and inventory details. The software product may have
multiple functions, but functionality is expressed as a totality of essential functions that the
software product provides.

G. Reliability
The set of attributes related to the capability of software to maintain its level of performance
under stated conditions for a stated period of time. The reliability characteristic tells the
stakeholders about how effectively and efficiently a software solution maintains the level of
performance if used under specified/stated conditions. Reliability can be used to evaluate the
performance of whole or part of software and based on that suggest corrective measures to
ensure continued software performance.

H. Usability
Usability can be defined as the ease to use any function especially from user view-point.
Usability refers to the set of attributes of any software solution related to the individual
assessment of different function by the stated users. The usability characteristic allows the
stakeholders to conclude about how easily the solutions can be learned, understood and used.
A good example to understand the concept is the revolutionary switch from Keyboard to touch-
screen in 2007, and that makes Steve Jobs quote “Machines can be user Friendly too” a reality.

Module-01: Software Quality Engineering Discipline

A. Quality Engineering Basics
What is software quality? What are the characteristics of high quality software solutions? What
defines quality? These are some of the subjective question in the field of Software Quality
Engineering. Modern Software Systems are usually interconnections of multiple underlying
software and due to lack of standardization and varied nature it’s really difficult to define
quality. Software Quality Engineering involves complete software development process just to
ensure that that any agreed-upon processes, standards and procedures are being followed to
get desired results and there should be no cherry picking of standards

B. Roles and Responsibility
People may have different expectations related to software quality assurance based on their
roles and responsibility. The stakeholders for software development are divided into two and
their expectations are as follows:

C. Consumer
Consumers of a software product are further categorized into the following:
   ● Users are the group which use the services acquired by the customer: The quality
     expectations on the side of users are as follows:
         o It performs all the functions as specified in the software requirements, which
             fits/meets the user’s needs.
         o Performs all the specified functions correctly over repeated use or over a long
             period of time, or performs its functions reliably.
   ● Customer usually acquire the Software and Services: The quality expectations on the
     side of consumer are as follows:
         o Basic expectations of the consumer are similar to that of users with additional
             concentration on the cost of the software solution.

D. Producer
Producer of the software solutions includes person involved in the development, management,
maintenance and service of the software product. It also includes third party software product
and organizations. For producers, the expectations are as follows:
   ● Their biggest concern is to fulfill their contractual obligations by producing software
     products that conform to product specifications.
   ● Proper choice of software methodologies, languages, tools, software usability and
     modifiability and other factors are closely related to quality for this category of
     stakeholders.
                                                                                      Page | 3

E. Off the Shelf Products
These are plug-and-play products and are usually known as Plugins. They are developed and
tested independently of Software Solutions. Their main purpose is to provide reusable
functionality. Off-the-shelf (OTS) software products can be defined as “software product(s)
available for any user, at cost or not, and used without the need to conduct development
activities”. Proper analysis should be perform while making decision regarding selection OTS as
one solution does not fit all.

   ISO-9126 Quality Framework
ISO-9126 is International Standard for Software Evaluation, it provides hierarchical framework
for quality definition, organized into quality characteristics. There are six top-level quality
characteristics that are summarized below:

F. Functionality
Functionality is the essential purpose of any product or service. The functionality characteristic
allows drawing conclusions about how well software provides and performs desired functions.
The functions are those that satisfy stated or implied needs. The more functions a product has,
e.g. a sale order processing system, then the more complicated it becomes to define it's
functionality. Continuing with the same example, the sales order system must be able to record
sales, price, quantity, tax, shipping and inventory details. The software product may have
multiple functions, but functionality is expressed as a totality of essential functions that the
software product provides.

G. Reliability
The set of attributes related to the capability of software to maintain its level of performance
under stated conditions for a stated period of time. The reliability characteristic tells the
stakeholders about how effectively and efficiently a software solution maintains the level of
performance if used under specified/stated conditions. Reliability can be used to evaluate the
performance of whole or part of software and based on that suggest corrective measures to
ensure continued software performance.

H. Usability
Usability can be defined as the ease to use any function especially from user view-point.
Usability refers to the set of attributes of any software solution related to the individual
assessment of different function by the stated users. The usability characteristic allows the
stakeholders to conclude about how easily the solutions can be learned, understood and used.
A good example to understand the concept is the revolutionary switch from Keyboard to touch-
screen in 2007, and that makes Steve Jobs quote “Machines can be user Friendly too” a reality.

CS611 ASSIGNMENT

Question-I

Suppose you are working as a software quality assurance engineer in a software house name XYZ Pvt. Ltd. Your company is developing point of sale “POS-Shop” for a grocery store. This system helps in smooth checkout for the customers and also this system maintain the inventory for the store. The implementation phase of the system has been completed and testing is underway.  You have to have to ensure the quality of the software you are developing.

During testing you found various problems in the software. Now you are required to classify these problems into errors, bugs, faults, defects and failures. You also have to provide solution for each.

Following tasks needs to be done.

A. Your task is to classify these problems into errors, bugs, faults, defects, and failures.
B. Also provide an explanation about your classification.
C. Propose solutions for each problem. Your solution include details about what needs to be done to fix the problem and prevent it from recurring?

    • Your task is to classify these problems into errors, bugs, faults, defects, and failures.
Problem 1: Users report that, during checkout, the total order cost is sometimes miscalculated and doesn't match the item prices in their cart.
Solution:
                Error
               Explained: This is a fault because the system is unable to effectively calculate the overall order cost.

Problem 2: When a customer adds an item to their wishlist, the system occasionally crashes, and an error message appears.
Solution:
Bugs :
Definition: This is a bug when the system frequently fails when an end user adds an item to its request.

Problem 3: In the product catalog, some items have missing images, even though they were uploaded by the administrator.
Solution:
Faults:
Explained: This is a bug that there is an error from expected behavior - photos are absent from the good's catalog notwithstanding being published.

Problem 4: Customers have encountered an issue where, upon attempting to log in, the system does not recognize their credentials and returns an "Invalid username or password" message. This occurs intermittently.
Solution:
Defect:
Explanation: This is an error caused by the computer's system failing to acknowledge acceptable privileges upon login, culminating in a "Inadmissible user or password" advance warning.

Problem 5: The search functionality works correctly most of the time, but occasionally it returns no results for valid queries.
Solution:
Failure:
Explanation: This is an outcome that the system is inconsistent with the criteria set forth. For valid searches, the search engine should frequently return responses.

    • Also provide an explanation about your classification.
Taxonomy Definition:

    • The bug:

Bugs represent programming mistakes which lead to unintended consequences. The overestimate of the total transaction cost in Problem 1 is a significant variation from the expected functioning, showing a fault in the code that does the calculation.

    • Fault:

Faults are defects in the functioning of a software program under particular conditions. The system crashing occasionally when adding items to the wishlist in Problem 2 indicates an error in the reliability of the system or execution of request-related actions.

    • Defects:

Defects are departures from the guidelines and anticipated behavior. In Problem 3, the missing images in the product catalog suggest a flaw since the system as a whole fails to show the images which the administrator had uploaded as planned.

    • Error:

Errors arise whenever an errors in the software leads to an incorrect outcome. Problem 4, in which the system fails to determine acceptable keys during login, is an error since it differs from the organized login behavior.

    • Failure:

Failures develop when the application fails to fulfill the minimum requirements. Problem 5 is a failure since the search capacity occasionally gives no results for acceptable inquiries, which does not always meet the stated goal of giving search results.

    •  Propose solutions for each problem. Your solution include details about what needs to be done to fix the problem and prevent it from recurring?

    • Bug(Problem 1 - Miscalculation of Total Order Cost):

Solution: Go over and over and fix the part of the code that calculates the entirety of the order cost. Implement thorough verification that guarantees precise numbers in a variety of settings.

    • Problem 2 (System Crashes Whenever Adding into The wish list):

Solution: Look at the stability of the system during wishlist operations. Identify and correct the code flaw that is causing those sporadic crashes. Implement extensive testing to ensure the stability of the wishlist functionality.

    • Defect (Problem 3 - Image Missing in Product Catalog):

Examine the image uploading and retrieval processes. Correct the code that is in charge of displaying photos in the good's catalog. Perform testing in order to guarantee that all supplied photos appear correctly.

    • Error (Problem 4 - Login Issue - Message "Inadmissible Account or Password"):

Solution: Go thru the username and password process for authentication again. Correct the code so that legitimate identification numbers are identified consistently. To check whether the issue has been successfully corrected, perform extensive testing using several login scenarios.

    • Failure (Problem 5 - Search Capability Returns No Results At times):

Assess the search algorithm and categorization methods. Resolve the problems that lead to irregular failures in the return of search results. Perform comprehensive testing in order to guarantee that the search functionality's trustworthiness.
